utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Stankovic and Gojko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I have the appearances. The Prosecutor first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and I appear here with my colleague Manoj Sachdeva, and we are accompanied by our case manager, van Hooydonk, Sebastian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. For the defendants. First, I see that you are alone, Mr. Koppe. Mr. Koppe, you are assigned counsel to Mr. Stankovic. I do see that Mr. Stankovic is not in the courtroom. We'll deal with that soon. Then for the accused Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Aleksandar Lazarevic, counsel for Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Before we continue, perhaps I should first raise the issue of the absence of Mr. Stankovic. I was informed that Mr. Stankovic refuses to enter this courtroom in the presence of Mr. Jankovic because he considers that he is entitled to have his own Status Conference and not together with Mr. Jankovic. Is that a correct understanding? I do not hear any confirmation. I can understand, Mr. Koppe, that in the present situation might not be easy for you to confirm such a thing because, from what I read, Mr. Stankovic's attitude towards you is rather hostile and perhaps does not allow you to confirm the information I received. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, of course, we have to deal with the matter. I go now in the history of this case where -- and please correct me when I'm wrong -- whether it's counsel for Mr. Jankovic or counsel for Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Stankovic has been indicted together with four others. That was a joint indictment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, it was, as far as I remember correctly, seven others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seven others.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then I forgot a few. I am aware -- so that was a joint indictment brought against all these accused under -- and charges were brought under Rule 48, which reads: "Persons accused of the same or different crimes committed in the course of the same transaction may be jointly charged and tried." That's joinder of accused. Joinder of crimes is not -- Rule 49 is not relevant at this moment. The defendants, having been charged jointly, are therefore in the same case. And unless there is a decision under Rule, I think it's 82, which would be an order for separate trials, then they are still in the same case. Was there ever any application for a separation or severance of trial?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must admit I cannot answer that question. According to my memory, there wasn't. But I may be wrong on this. And we are trying at the moment to find a decision because my colleague Mr. Sachdeva seems to recall that there was a decision of severance. But he also isn't sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm aware of is that in the second amended indictment, that it was -- the Prosecution presented in its argument that it would leave out any reference to any other accused, and therefore on from the second amended indictment we see that it's only the name of Mr. Stankovic that appears, which in itself might not mean that this is the same as an order for separate trial. But if you could further inform me, Mr. -- Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff or Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think my colleague who was on that Stankovic case could easier answer the question than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May it please you. We did seek to amend the second amended indictment and just place Mr. Stankovic separately in the indictment. And following that, we sought to amend again the second amended indictment, which resulted in a decision which confirmed a third amended indictment against Radovan Stankovic where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That third amended indictment was filed on the 8th of December, 2003, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct. And I understand a decision was -- was rendered on the 24th of February, 2004, if I'm not mistaken. And that, as I understand it, is how the -- how it stands -- how the case stands against Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So do I have to understand this, that there's no severance -- the cases were not severed, although the indictment now only names Mr. Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I understand that's correct, that there was no formal decision on severance. However, there is an indictment confirmed separately against Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which -- then, Mr. Lazarevic, I know that you are not representing Mr. Stankovic, but of course your client is one of the candidates for being in a joint case with Mr. Stankovic. What -- what's your view on that, and since Mr. Jankovic is here and has not refused to appear together with Mr. Stankovic, what's your view?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the only thing I can say is that I share my client's position. He definitely has no problem of being here at this moment. But the indictment that I was dealing with was the initial indictment, the first indictment with seven persons on it, so I'm not aware of any decision regarding severance of trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we started today this Status Conference - because I should have noted that we are in a Status Conference at this moment - I asked the Registry to convey the message to Mr. Stankovic that if he would appear - and that would be to appear together with Mr. Jankovic - that I would have given him a couple of minutes right in the beginning of this hearing to explain why he considers these cases to be separate cases rather than joint cases. I learned from the representative of the Registry that Mr. Stankovic refused even to enter the courtroom even if such an opportunity would be given to him. Under the present circumstances, where there is no clarity and where Mr. Stankovic seems not to wish to contribute to clarify the issue, we will continue with this Status Conference even in the absence of Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Koppe, you are assigned as counsel, so you're the one who represents to the best of your abilities, and I do understand the problems, but you are the one who represents the interests of Mr. Stankovic at this moment during this hearing. If at any later stage any of the parties would have a different view on whether these cases are joint cases or not, I'd like to hear. If Mr. Stankovic would for whatever reason consider it inappropriate to be in a joint case with Mr. Jankovic, he will be in a position to apply for a severance of the cases. And the Registry is instructed to convey this message in a language the accused understands to him. We'll now continue with the Status Conference. The first issue is the application Mr. Stankovic in some letters made that he wants to represent himself. If Mr. Stankovic would have been present at this moment, I would have explained to him again the reasons why his former counsel -- why assignment of former counsel was withdrawn, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that is, for reasons of financial misconduct. I would then have asked Mr. Stankovic, because that's not entirely clear from the letters he sent to the Chamber, whether it's his wish to represent himself is mainly because he does not want to be represented by counsel presently assigned, that is, Mr. Koppe, and that he would withdraw an application for self-representation apart from whether the formalities were fulfilled if another counsel of the list but, of course, not his former counsel, Mr. Radovic, would be assigned. We don't have that information at this moment; therefore, we'll wait and see whether that information will reach the Chamber. In view of the two options that were in the mind of the Chamber, I would say the following: If Mr. Stankovic would withdraw his wish to represent himself if other counsel would be assigned to him, the appropriate way of proceeding would be that he applies with the Registrar for replacement of counsel. Whether that would be granted is a different matter, but that's the way it should be done. If, however, Mr. Stankovic would not accept any other counsel than the one that previously was assigned but whose assignment was withdrawn, then the Chamber would be hesitant to accept self-representation for the reasons that obstructionist and abusive behaviour might give a reason to make an exception to the right of a defendant to represent himself. In the present situation where Mr. Stankovic is not present, I will refrain from taking any decision, but matter has been considered within the Chamber. I finally make the following observation: That whatever this Chamber would decide in terms of self-representation or being represented by counsel, by assigned counsel, then that is totally separate from what the Appeals Chamber will do in the 11 bis proceedings pending at this moment. Is there any need to make any further submissions related to what I just said, in relation to self-representation sought by Mr. Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would, of course, not object to -- to the fact if Mr. Stankovic would select a different counsel, probably a counsel that speaks his language. We wouldn't have objections against this idea. But, of course, we would have considerable objections against his self-representation. And, Your Honour, if you want me to address these considerable concerns now, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I can also do that in writing at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit hesitant. The way in which the matter has been introduced, that is, sending a letter to the Judges and say, "I don't want Mr. Koppe" -- and, Mr. Koppe, you may have noticed that the terms in which Mr. Stankovic describes you are not the most elegant ones, to say it briefly. That's of course not a way to introduce such a matter. At the same time, on this Status Conference I could address the matter because it deals with practicalities and not only with formal requests. The first thing the Chamber will do is whether -- to determine whether there's a formal request for self-representation or whether there's not. And if we would consider the request for self-representation to be introduced in such a manner that we could further consider it, then you're invited, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, the Prosecution is invited to give its view on the self-representation. Thank you for your observations. Mr. Koppe, any ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have a few things to say. I -- I wish to say to you that I do find myself in quite an awkward position. On the one hand, I am -- I should be representing the interests of Mr. Stankovic to the best of my ability and knowledge; on the other hand, it's clear that Mr. Stankovic doesn't want me to represent him. I have been asked by the Registrar at one point in time - I believe it was sometime in April - to represent Mr. Stankovic solely on the matter of the appeals -- appeal against the decision on the 11 bis ruling. As you are undoubtedly aware, this procedure has almost finished in respect of the appeal and the brief of -- the appeal brief, which should have been finally filed by yesterday. So it seems to me that if there are no oral arguments at one point in time, that the -- the representation requested by the Registrar seems almost finished. And it is my inclination that I would like to request withdrawal as an assigned counsel at one point in time and that -- the reason that I'm here now is solely because of the fact that the appeals procedure is still formally pending. But summarising, it is, once again, for me awkward and strange to stand here and represent Mr. Stankovic in the clear view that he doesn't want my assistance. These are just the few observations I would like to make at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Koppe. I do understand your position to be a very difficult one. It's a position in which counsel would not wish to be in. At the same time, I do hear that you might soon apply for a withdrawal of your assignment as counsel. At the same time, you may also be aware -- and first of all, that is a matter for the Registry to decide and not for the Chamber -- and that there is at least, to say it frankly, some tension between accepting withdrawal and not accepting if the Chamber would not accept self-representation by Mr. Stankovic, so therefore the two are related and therefore I can't promise you that whatever action you take, that you're out of trouble immediately. Then, Mr. Lazarevic, do you have to add anything to this? I think it's not related directly to your client, so it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the second point on the agenda. The Chamber has become aware that an appeal brief has been filed in the 11 bis proceedings. If there's anything more to be said about it, of course this Chamber is not seized of any appeal nor seized of the 11 bis application, because it's exclusively the Referral Bench who deals with that. Any need to make any further observations in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, of course there's also pending a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not an appeal but an 11 bis application is pending for Mr. Jankovic. Is there anything in relation to that, not the substance of it, because that's before the Referral Bench, but is there any observation to be made in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we are mindful that this Status Conference is not held on this issue, that this Chamber is not designed for 11 bis proceedings, so nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I come to my next point, and that is the application for provisional release filed on behalf of Mr. Jankovic. You've set out the reasons why the Defence considers it appropriate to provisionally release Mr. Jankovic. We have not yet received the response from the Prosecution. There are two ways to deal with it: We either could invite the Prosecution to file its response. We also could give an opportunity to the Prosecution to orally respond to the application at this moment. Mr. Lazarevic, would you oppose against any of the options?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course not, Your Honour. I mean, according to the Rules, the Prosecution is entitled to give its response in whatever way they find appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if -- if you'd say, "No, that should not be done orally," then I would like at least to know that. But since there's no objection, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, what would you prefer to, to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. respond, in writing or orally?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution is currently already preparing our response in writing, and I assume it can be filed this week or beginning -- beginning next week. So I would prefer to give a considered and well-formulated opinion on the provisional release. Of course I can say today that we are opposing it, but I actually would -- would like to file a -- a well-considered response. And it's on its way. Actually, it's being prepared at the moment, as we speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we could expect that still this week, as I understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's very likely that we'll file on Friday, but it could also be next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll respect the preference expressed by the Prosecution. Of course, the Chamber will -- once we have received the response, will consider the application and give a decision in due course. Then the next point on the agenda is an application made by the Prosecution, as far as I understand, to stay the determination of a motion challenging the form of the indictment. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, the application by the Defence was filed on the 12th of May, 2005 and the Prosecution on the 23rd of May filed a motion requesting halt of the decision on the motion until the decision on 11 bis is filed. Should the case remain before this Trial Chamber, the Prosecution would amend the indictment in form, not in substance, however. It is an indictment originating from 1997, and therefore we would like to amend the form of the indictment and make it consistent with the findings in the Kunarac case and the jurisprudence on the form of the indictment within these almost -- almost nine years. Many of the objections of the Defence relate to vagueness of the indictment and a lack of particulars, and we would like to address it in an amendment. The charges and the scope of the indictment, however, would remain absolutely the same. That's why we think the amendment would not have any impact on the decision on 11 bis that is pending before the transfer chamber. If 11 bis is granted, there would be no need at all to amend the indictment in this institution here. The Prosecutor in the Sarajevo State Court would have to amend the indictment to -- related to their charging practice there and the provisions that they would have to deal with. I think if we would be ordered to amend the indictment now, we -- we would delay proceedings and we would actually have to do unnecessary work because in the event that it is transferred -- the case is transferred, our work wouldn't really have an impact on the decisions and the dealings of the Prosecutor in Sarajevo. And if the case stays here in The Hague, then amendment would have to be done and there would be enough time to do it after the decision is known. Therefore, I would ask you to grant our motion to keep the decision on the preliminary motion of the Defence in abeyance until the time on the 11 bis decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, from the answer of Madam Uertz, I take it that vagueness is not a problem when a case has to be referred but vagueness might be at least -- you have filed your motion on the 12th of May, that vagueness is a problem in trying the case here. Could you -- I have some difficulties in understanding why vagueness in the one context would not cause a problem and in the other it would. Although, of course, I'm aware that an indictment could be reformulated if a case is referred. But could you give your views on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. I understand fully the position of the Prosecution. There are basically two ways that this case will go on in future: One is, well, whether 11 bis filing is granted. In such a situation, the case will be referred to Sarajevo and the national prosecution will file a completely new indictment. So the Prosecution feels obviously that it would be a work -- that the work on the indictment would be done without any good reason. On the other hand, in -- if the case stays in The Hague, they are ready to file a new indictment. That's basically the way I understand the Prosecutor's situation. But the reasons that were given for not amending the indictment are basically the same that have to do with the previous issue that we were dealing with, and this is the provisional release. Basically the -- it also has an impact -- the 11 bis proceedings would also have an impact and still the Prosecution is ready to file a motion and its response to our filing. So basically what we wanted to say and all the issues that we raised in our motion on the form of the indictment remained the same. We are leaving all these to the Trial Chamber to decide, to determine whether the Prosecution request is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand you well that you say you do not take any firm position on the matter since both options - the one is that - not -- well, the option that we would wait and see what the Referral Chamber does is -- whether or not the preferred one is not an unacceptable one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, basically we would prefer to have a new indictment, but of course it's up to the Trial Chamber to determine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I do understand. It's the Chamber that decides. But I would like to find out how strong your position is -- how strong your preference is. And that is the need to have the -- to have a decision on the amendment of the indictment even if the case would be referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I have just stated we would like to have an amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say it's -- I consider this to be a slight preference for amendment to the proceedings on the amendment to be continued. Madam Uertz, you say it's -- it's double work to deal with the amendment of the indictment. Would you fear any problems if the Stankovic and the Jankovic indictment would be entirely -- would it bother you if there would still be that much difference in view of a referral?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- it wouldn't bother me, because when you look at the indictment, the -- the rapes that are actually related to this accused here, Mr. Jankovic, are not the same ones that Mr. Stankovic is charged with. So I can't really see why that should be a problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- at all. Because looking at the Stankovic indictment, that's basically conduct that relates to the Karaman's House in Miljevina, while the conduct of Mr. Jankovic, his -- his participation is related to other places, like Buk Bijela, like Partizan -- Partizan and Foca High School. So they -- the indictment would always look different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Because it's simply a different conduct that they -- they are accused of. And to address, again, the matter of vagueness and lack of particulars. I -- I would say the indictment is still in the margin that would be sufficient here, but of course if we get the -- the order to amend the indictment or whether we have an opportunity to amend the indictment, we would simply add more details on, in particular, his role as commander and his -- his role as a leading soldier, a soldier leading others, because that -- at that time, when we filed the indictment, all the details that we later learned in the Foca cases that were conducted here in this Court gave us a lot more details on this position. And that, we could add. And that's what we wanted to add in case we have to amend the indictment. The crimes as such as they are described, they are very detailed. They're already described in a lot of details. And these crimes, we wouldn't add to. But just to his role as a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz. Any further need to respond to that, Mr. Lazarevic? If not, then I'll move to the next subject, which would be the -- any concerns about the health of the accused at this moment or their detention conditions. Mr. Koppe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: I cannot say anything obviously about his present health situation because I have never spoken to my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since he's not in the courtroom, we can't even observe whether he looks healthy or not at this moment. Mr. Lazarevic, in respect of Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe it would be more appropriate that Mr. Jankovic states for himself what is his health condition. I'm not aware of any particular problems that Mr. Jankovic might have in the Detention Unit, but of course he could say that for himself in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- a more -- much better way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you have an opportunity to address me in relation to any health matter or any detention matter. If there would be any need to turn into private session because you consider the matter to be such that they should not be available to the public, you may indicate so and then I'll decide whether or not to go in private session. Please say what you'd like to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Detention Unit is concerned, I'm absolutely satisfied with everything. I wouldn't single out anything. I am completely satisfied with everything. As for as my personal health is concerned, when you look at me, I look healthy; however, my health is rather impaired. All of my internal bodily organs -- only my left kidney is healthy. My lungs don't work properly; my heart neither; the liver; the prostate. I should have been operated on the prostate a year and a half ago. In my left -- right heart I have a bullet fragment that should have been taken out. I suffered two minor coronaries and I still have problems with my heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you describe health problems you're facing at this moment. You also say, "I should have gone -- undergone surgery already for quite some time ago." Should I understand this as that you do not receive the proper care or that there are other reasons why you could not receive such treatment at this moment? For example, I can imagine that taking out a bullet fragment from, as you say, your right heart - it's good to se that persons have two hearts - but I take it the right portion of your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was diagnosed at the military academy in Belgrade in Yugoslavia. The fragment cannot be taken out. I was in a state of clinical death, and I had to be -- undergo RCP [as interpreted] while this was happening. The fragment has to stay there. And as far as the prostate surgery is concerned, it was said a year and a half ago that I should be operated on. However, I was treated with some teas that I received from the former Yugoslavia, and recently I have run out of that tea or herbal remedy, so I have again within suffering from nocturnal pains. I have to go to the bathroom more often than usually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Lazarevic, if there would be any problem to the extent that Mr. Jankovic would not receive the medical treatment he's entitled to, that you would bring that first of all to the attention of the Registrar and, of course, if that doesn't resolve anything, finally the Chamber might be in a position - I'm cautious to say that - might be in a position to -- to deal with the matter also. But you know the procedure. The procedure is the Registrar is responsible for the Detention Unit and only if it affects the trial or if there is an explicit right to ask review of any decision of the Registrar, you can address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour. I am fully aware of the procedure. What I can inform the Trial Chamber is that I have just brought from Belgrade a complete medical record of Mr. Jankovic, so the Detention Unit will have a complete medical record. And if anything goes wrong for Mr. Jankovic, he will definitely inform me and I will undertake all the measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jankovic, of course the Chamber and I feel sorry to hear about your medical problems. You may be seated, unless you would like to add anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other matter to be raised at this moment? Madam Uertz.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Perhaps a -- I can again be of assistance in the original question a little bit more now, on the original question of whether the cases are still joined or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Because in the Kunarac case a similar situation arose. Kunarac was arrested a long time before the other two, and his indictment was amended considerably. And when the other two accused were finally here in The Hague, a decision was made on joining the trial, the trials against the three. So decision on joinder of trials, a formal decision was made on the 15th of February, 2000 in the case IT-96-23-PT. Obviously the Trial Chamber at that time found that the cases had to be joined formally. That means that they thought they were separated from Kunarac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do understand that the initial situation where several accused were jointly indicted was then changed to the extent that the Kunarac case was at least severed from the others and the others were joined, or should I say, joined again. Let there be no doubt: If it would appear - but we'll pay further attention to it - if it would appear that the cases could not be considered to be joined case, then a new Status Conference will be scheduled to have a separate scheduled -- Status Conference for Mr. Stankovic. But in the present situation, I have insufficient reasons to schedule such a separate Status Conference. Any other matter, Madam Uertz?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Koppe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOPPE
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes this Status Conference.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
